function: Learned joint control of DL beamforming, RIS phase shifts, DL power allocation and UL transmit power, maximizing the minimum beampattern gain under UL/DL rate constraints (p. 1, 7).
system: Full-duplex BS with Nt=Nr=6 antennas, single-antenna users, reflecting phase-only RIS (ULA, M=16-100 elements), NOMA, 3 sensing targets, 24 GHz carrier (p. 4, 7, 12-13).
method: Multi-agent PPO: DL and UL actors (two 128-unit layers) with shared critic, centralized training, decentralized execution; online reinforcement learning with GAE (p. 8-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: Rician BS-RIS and RIS-user links with CN(0,I) NLoS, CN(0,1) user-user links, 3GPP TR 38.901 UMi path loss only; no dataset or measurements (p. 5, 7).
test_conditions: Agents trained online and evaluated in the same simulated setting; results swept over RIS elements, users, antennas, SI level and fading dynamics; no unseen-condition test stated (p. 12-15).
baselines: Non-learned: random-search heuristic. Learned: single-agent PPO, QMIX (Fig. 3 only). Half-duplex versions of MA-PPO and PPO compared with full-duplex (p. 11-13).
metrics: Minimum beampattern gain, DL/UL/total sum-rate, total reward and convergence episodes, beam pattern versus angle (p. 12-15).
complexity: Orders per step: environment O(K^2 Nt M+U^2 Nr M+Nt M^2), actor O(S*H+H^2+H*A), critic O(S*H+H^2), H=128; no runtime or FLOPs (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 5: "the large-scale pathloss is modeled separately according to the 3GPP standard"; p. 7: "we follow 3GPP TR 38.901 for the Urban Micro (UMi) Street-Canyon environment" but only the path-loss formula follows, and the small-scale links are custom Rician ("the Rician factor quantifying the dominance of the LoS component") with CN(0, I) NLoS. No CDL/TDL, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO or measured data, so not met.
q2_support: p. 13: "Fig. 7 shows the comparison of the minimum beam pattern gain of the PPO and MA-PPO algorithms in FD and HD modes with varying numbers of RIS elements"; p. 12: "With 2000 training episodes and 25 steps per episode". Only sweeps of M, users, antennas and SI level are shown; the paper never states a model trained in one condition and tested in another.
q3_support: p. 11: "we employ a heuristic method implemented through random search" (non-learned); p. 12: "compared with PPO, a heuristic baseline, and QMIX"; p. 13: "MA-PPO framework in comparison with PPO and heuristic baselines for optimizing the minimum beampattern gain"; p. 4: "A preliminary study was reported in [62], where a single-agent DRL-based optimization framework was introduced".
q4_support: p. 11: "the overall environment complexity per step can be expressed as" O(K^2 Nt M + U^2 Nr M + Nt M^2); p. 11: "The per-step computational complexity of the actor network is" O(S*H + H^2 + H*A_PPO), critic O(S*H + H^2).
q5_support: p. 12: "The simulations were implemented in Python 3.12 using the Spyder IDE, with PyTorch 2.4.1 (CPU version)"; no code or data link is given anywhere and the channels come from the authors' own simulator (p. 7), not a public dataset, so not met.
notes: Include; first page (p. 1) holds the title Multi-Agent PPO-Based Resource Optimization for Full-Duplex RIS-Aided NOMA-ISAC Systems, matching the DOI. Passes steps 1-7: PPO learns beamforming, RIS phases and powers (physical layer), BS has 6 antennas plus RIS, results are simulated (p. 12-15). Area 5 rather than 3 by the specificity order, since the objective is the minimum beampattern gain toward targets under communication rate constraints (p. 7). Judgement calls for the reviewer: q1 is 0 because only the UMi path loss comes from TR 38.901, fading is custom Rician; q3 is 1 with the random-search heuristic as non-learned baseline and single-agent PPO (the authors' earlier single-agent DRL, p. 4) plus QMIX (Fig. 3, total reward only) as learned baselines, so the reviewer should confirm that single-agent PPO is not read as an ablation of MA-PPO.
